rules.rule_name: Program Initialization - Open All Required Files
rules.rule_description: Before any processing begins, the program must successfully open all five required files: Transaction Category Balance (input), Cross-Reference (input), Disclosure Group (input), Account Master (input/output), and Transaction Output (output). Processing cannot proceed if any file fails to open.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Open Transaction Category Balance File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C is starting execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Category Balance File, Cross-Reference File, Disclosure Group File, Account Master File, and Transaction Output File in sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: All five files must be successfully opened before any record processing begins; the Transaction Category Balance File and Cross-Reference File and Disclosure Group File are opened for input only, the Account Master File is opened for both reading and updating, and the Transaction Output File is opened for writing new records

rules.rule_name: Sequential Reading of Transaction Category Balance Records
rules.rule_description: The program reads transaction category balance records one at a time in sequential order from the Transaction Category Balance File. Each record contains an Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, and a balance amount that will be used for interest calculation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Transaction Category Balance Record Reading
Read Next Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance File has been successfully opened and the program is in its main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Transaction Category Balance File sequentially
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a record is successfully read, the record count is incremented by 1 and the record is displayed, and processing continues with account change detection; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set to 'Y' and the final account update is triggered

rules.rule_name: Account Change Detection
rules.rule_description: Since transaction category balance records are grouped by Account ID, the program must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the previously processed Account ID. This signals that all records for the prior account have been processed and a new account's records are beginning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Account Change Detection
Account ID Changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read and the program has a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is compared to the last processed Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account IDs are different, an account change is detected and the program must finalize the prior account before initializing for the new account; if the Account IDs are the same, the program proceeds directly to interest rate lookup for the current record

rules.rule_name: First Record Processed Detection
rules.rule_description: When an account change is detected, the program must determine whether this is the very first account being processed. On the first account, there is no prior account to update, so the account update step must be skipped. The first-time flag is initialized to 'Y' and set to 'N' after the first account is encountered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
First Record
Processed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account change has been detected on the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-FIRST-TIME is 'Y' (this is the first account encountered), the prior account update is skipped and WS-FIRST-TIME is set to 'N'; if WS-FIRST-TIME is 'N' (a prior account exists), the prior account balance update is performed before processing the new account

rules.rule_name: Account Interest Accumulation Reset for New Account
rules.rule_description: When processing begins for a new account, the total interest accumulator must be reset to zero to ensure that interest calculated for the new account is not contaminated by interest amounts from the previously processed account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Account Interest Accumulation Reset
Reset Total Interest to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account change has been detected and either the prior account has been updated or this is the first account being processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes processing for the new account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is reset to zero, the new Account ID is saved as the current Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM), and the Account ID is set as the key for subsequent Account Master and Cross-Reference file lookups

rules.rule_name: Account Master Data Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a new account is encountered, the program retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key. The account record provides the current balance, account group ID, and cycle credit/debit amounts needed for interest application and account update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Account Data Retrieval
Retrieve Account Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been identified from the transaction category balance record and the Account Master File is open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the Account Master File using the Account ID (FD-ACCT-ID) as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account is found, the full account record including current balance, account group ID, current cycle credits, and current cycle debits is loaded into memory for use in subsequent processing; if the account is not found, a message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: [Account ID]' is displayed

rules.rule_name: Card Cross-Reference Lookup for Account
rules.rule_description: When a new account is encountered, the program retrieves the card cross-reference record using the Account ID as the lookup key. The cross-reference record provides the Card Number associated with the account, which is required as a field on every interest transaction record written to the output file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Card Cross-Reference Lookup
Retrieve Card Number for Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master record has been retrieved for the new account and the Cross-Reference File is open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the cross-reference record is found, the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) associated with the account is loaded into memory for use when writing interest transaction records; if the account is not found in the cross-reference file, a message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: [Account ID]' is displayed

rules.rule_name: Interest Rate Lookup by Account Group, Transaction Category, and Transaction Type
rules.rule_description: For each transaction category balance record, the applicable annual interest rate is looked up from the Disclosure Group File using a composite key of Account Group ID, Transaction Category Code, and Transaction Type Code. This determines the rate to apply to the specific balance category for the account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Interest Rate Lookup by Account Group
Lookup Interest Rate by Group/Type/Category

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master record has been retrieved providing the Account Group ID, and the current transaction category balance record provides the Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the Disclosure Group File using the composite key of Account Group ID (FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID) + Transaction Category Code (FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD) + Transaction Type Code (FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a matching disclosure group record is found, the interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) from that record is used for interest calculation; if no matching record is found, the program falls back to the default interest rate lookup

rules.rule_name: Default Interest Rate Fallback When Specific Rate Not Found
rules.rule_description: When no interest rate record exists for the specific Account Group, Transaction Category, and Transaction Type combination, the program retries the lookup using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID while keeping the same Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code. This ensures a fallback rate is always available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Default Interest Rate Fallback
Retry with DEFAULT Group Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group File lookup using the specific Account Group ID returned no matching record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program retries the Disclosure Group File lookup with the Account Group ID overridden to 'DEFAULT' while retaining the original Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The interest rate from the DEFAULT disclosure group record is used for the interest calculation for this transaction category balance record; if the DEFAULT record is also not found, a processing error is raised

rules.rule_name: Zero Interest Rate Skip Rule
rules.rule_description: If the interest rate retrieved from the Disclosure Group File (either specific or default) is zero, no interest calculation and no fee calculation is performed for that transaction category balance record. The program skips directly to reading the next record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Interest Rate
Not Zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An interest rate has been retrieved from the Disclosure Group File for the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates whether the retrieved interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) is equal to zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the interest rate is zero, both the interest calculation and the fee calculation are skipped entirely and the program reads the next transaction category balance record; if the interest rate is greater than zero, the program proceeds to calculate monthly interest

rules.rule_name: Monthly Interest Calculation Formula
rules.rule_description: When a non-zero interest rate exists, the monthly interest charge for a transaction category balance is calculated by multiplying the category balance by the annual interest rate and dividing by 1200. Dividing by 1200 converts the annual percentage rate to a monthly decimal rate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Monthly Interest Calculation
Monthly Interest = 
'Category Balance × Rate' / 1200

acceptance_criteria.Given: A non-zero interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) has been retrieved and the transaction category balance (TRAN-CAT-BAL) is available from the current record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program computes the monthly interest for the transaction category
acceptance_criteria.Then: Monthly Interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT) is calculated as: (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) divided by 1200

rules.rule_name: Total Interest Accumulation Across Transaction Categories
rules.rule_description: The monthly interest calculated for each transaction category balance record is added to a running total for the current account. This accumulates interest across all transaction categories and transaction types belonging to the same account before the account balance is updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Total Interest Accumulation
Add Monthly Interest to
Running Account Total

acceptance_criteria.Given: Monthly interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been calculated for the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program adds the monthly interest to the account-level interest accumulator
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is increased by the computed monthly interest amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT), representing the cumulative interest across all processed transaction categories for the current account

rules.rule_name: Interest Transaction Record Creation
rules.rule_description: For every transaction category balance where interest is computed, a system-generated interest transaction record is written to the Transaction Output File. The record captures the interest charge with standardized codes identifying it as a system-generated interest transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Interest Transaction Record Creation
Create Transaction Record
Type=01, Category=05, Source=System
With Card Number and Timestamps

acceptance_criteria.Given: Monthly interest has been calculated and the Transaction ID has been generated for the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.When: The program creates and writes an interest transaction record to the Transaction Output File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction record is written with: Transaction ID set to the generated ID, Transaction Type Code set to '01', Transaction Category Code set to '05', Transaction Source set to 'System', Transaction Description set to 'Int. for a/c ' concatenated with the Account ID, Transaction Amount set to the computed monthly interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT), Merchant ID set to zero, Merchant Name left blank, Merchant City left blank, Merchant ZIP left blank, Card Number set to the card number retrieved from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM), Original Timestamp set to the current system timestamp, and Processing Timestamp set to the current system timestamp

rules.rule_name: Transaction ID Generation for Interest Transactions
rules.rule_description: Each interest transaction written to the output file must have a unique Transaction ID. The ID is constructed by combining a processing date parameter with an auto-incrementing numeric suffix that increases by one for each transaction written during the program run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Transaction ID Generation
Combine Processing Date +
Incrementing Suffix

acceptance_criteria.Given: An interest transaction is about to be written to the Transaction Output File
acceptance_criteria.When: The program generates the Transaction ID for the interest transaction record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is formed by concatenating the processing date parameter (PARM-DATE) with the current value of the transaction suffix counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), where WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is incremented by 1 before each transaction is written, ensuring each transaction receives a unique identifier

rules.rule_name: Fee Calculation Placeholder
rules.rule_description: The program includes a fee calculation step that is invoked after interest is computed for any transaction category balance record with a non-zero interest rate. However, the fee calculation logic has not yet been implemented and currently performs no action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Fee Calculation
Placeholder - Not Yet Implemented

acceptance_criteria.Given: Monthly interest has been calculated and the interest transaction record has been written for a transaction category balance record with a non-zero interest rate
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the fee calculation step
acceptance_criteria.Then: No fee calculation is performed at this time as the fee logic is not yet implemented; the program proceeds to read the next transaction category balance record

rules.rule_name: Account Balance Update - Apply Accumulated Interest and Reset Cycle Amounts
rules.rule_description: After all transaction category balance records for an account have been processed, the account's current balance is increased by the total accumulated interest for that account, and the current cycle credit and debit amounts are both reset to zero. The updated account record is then saved back to the Account Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Account Balance Update
Add Total Interest to Balance
Reset Cycle Credit/Debit to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records for the current account have been processed and the total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) holds the sum of all monthly interest amounts for that account
acceptance_criteria.When: The program finalizes processing for the account and updates the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) is increased by the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT); the current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is set to zero; the current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is set to zero; and the updated account record is written back to the Account Master File

rules.rule_name: Final Account Update at End of File
rules.rule_description: When the end of the Transaction Category Balance File is reached, the last account being processed must still receive its balance update. Since the account update is normally triggered by detecting a new account on the next record, a special end-of-file handler ensures the final account is not skipped.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Final Account Update
Update Last Account Balance

acceptance_criteria.Given: The end of the Transaction Category Balance File has been reached and the last account's transaction category balance records have all been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected in the main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account balance update is performed for the last account: the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), the current cycle credit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero, the current cycle debit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero, and the updated account record is saved to the Account Master File before the program proceeds to close all files

rules.rule_name: Program Completion - Close All Files
rules.rule_description: Upon completion of all record processing, the program must close all five files in sequence: Transaction Category Balance File, Cross-Reference File, Disclosure Group File, Account Master File, and Transaction Output File. All files must be properly closed before the program terminates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Program Completion
Close All Files

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records have been processed and the final account balance has been updated
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes its main processing loop and proceeds to termination
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Balance File is closed, followed by the Cross-Reference File, then the Disclosure Group File, then the Account Master File, and finally the Transaction Output File; after all files are successfully closed, the program terminates normally

rules.rule_description: The interest calculation program CBACT04C must announce its start before any file operations or processing begins, providing an audit trail of program execution.

acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution

rules.rule_name: Open Transaction Category Balance File for Reading
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Category Balance file, which contains the balance amounts per transaction category and type for each account, must be successfully opened in read-only mode before interest calculation processing can begin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Transaction Category Balance File for Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C has started execution and is in the initialization phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Category Balance file for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Cross-Reference file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION CATEGORY BALANCE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

rules.rule_name: Open Cross-Reference File for Reading
rules.rule_description: The Cross-Reference file, which maps Account IDs to Card Numbers and is required for populating interest transaction records, must be successfully opened in read-only mode as part of program initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Cross-Reference File for Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file has been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Cross-Reference file for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Disclosure Group file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE' along with the file status value, records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

rules.rule_name: Open Disclosure Group File for Reading
rules.rule_description: The Disclosure Group file, which contains the interest rates applicable per account group, transaction category, and transaction type, must be successfully opened in read-only mode as part of program initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Disclosure Group File for Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file and Cross-Reference file have been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Disclosure Group file for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Account Master file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

rules.rule_name: Open Account Master File for Reading and Updating
rules.rule_description: The Account Master file must be opened in both read and update mode (not read-only) because the program must both retrieve current account balances and write back updated balances after interest is applied. This dual-access mode is a critical business requirement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Account Master File for Reading and Updating

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, and Disclosure Group files have been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Master file for both reading and updating
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully in read-update mode, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Transaction Output file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT MASTER FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

rules.rule_name: Open Transaction Output File for Writing
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Output file, which will receive newly generated interest transaction records created during processing, must be successfully opened in write-only mode as the final step of program initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Transaction Output File for Writing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, and Account Master files have all been successfully opened and the program is completing initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Output file for writing
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to the main interest calculation processing loop; if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

rules.rule_name: Mandatory Sequential File Opening Order
rules.rule_description: All five required files must be opened in a strict, mandatory sequence during program initialization. Each file must be successfully opened before the next file opening is attempted. Interest calculation processing may only begin after all five files are confirmed open and ready.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Files Ready Proceed to Interest Calculation Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C has started execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs its initialization phase
acceptance_criteria.Then: The files must be opened in the following strict sequence: (1) Transaction Category Balance file for reading, (2) Cross-Reference file for reading, (3) Disclosure Group file for reading, (4) Account Master file for reading and updating, (5) Transaction Output file for writing; each file must open successfully before the next is attempted; if any file fails to open, the program terminates immediately without attempting to open subsequent files; only after all five files are successfully opened does the program proceed to interest calculation processing

rules.rule_name: All Files Must Be Available Before Processing Begins
rules.rule_description: Interest calculation processing is a dependent workflow — it requires all five data sources and output destinations to be available simultaneously. If any single file is unavailable, the entire interest calculation run must be aborted to prevent partial or inconsistent results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Files Ready Proceed to Interest Calculation Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C is initializing for an interest calculation run
acceptance_criteria.When: Any one of the five required files — Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, or Transaction Output — cannot be successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must not proceed to interest calculation processing under any circumstances; the program must display a descriptive error message identifying which file failed to open, display the diagnostic file status information, and terminate abnormally; this policy ensures no partial interest calculations are performed with incomplete data sources

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Transaction Category Balance Record from File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance File has been successfully opened and the End-of-File flag is set to 'N' (not yet reached end of file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next available transaction category balance record from the Transaction Category Balance File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next transaction category balance record is retrieved and loaded into the transaction category balance record buffer, making its data (Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Balance) available for subsequent interest calculation processing

rules.rule_name: Successful Record Read Validation
rules.rule_description: After each read attempt from the Transaction Category Balance File, the system determines whether a valid record was retrieved or whether the end of the file has been reached, directing the program flow accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Successfully Read?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Transaction Category Balance File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read was successful (file status = '00'), the record is considered valid and processing continues with incrementing the record counter and displaying the record; if the end of file has been reached (file status = '10'), the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y' and the final account update is triggered; if any other file status is returned, the read is treated as a file read error

rules.rule_name: Record Counter Increment on Successful Read
rules.rule_description: Each time a valid transaction category balance record is successfully read, the program increments a running counter to track the total number of records processed during the execution.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Record Counter

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read from the Transaction Category Balance File (End-of-File flag remains 'N')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the record was read without error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record counter (WS-RECORD-COUNT) is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly processed record

rules.rule_name: Display of Transaction Category Balance Record Details
rules.rule_description: After a valid transaction category balance record is read and counted, the full content of the record is displayed to provide an audit trail of all records being processed during program execution.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Record Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read and the record counter has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds with processing the record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete transaction category balance record content (including Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Balance amount) is displayed as part of the processing audit trail

rules.rule_name: Pass Valid Record to Interest Calculation Processing
rules.rule_description: After a transaction category balance record has been read, counted, and displayed, it is passed forward to the interest calculation processing stage where account data is retrieved and interest is computed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass Record to Interest Calculation Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read, the record counter has been incremented, and the record details have been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the record reading and logging steps
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction category balance record data (Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Balance) is made available to the interest calculation processing stage, which evaluates account changes, retrieves account and cross-reference data, looks up interest rates, and computes interest charges

rules.rule_name: End of File Detection and Flag Setting
rules.rule_description: When no more transaction category balance records are available in the file, the system marks the End-of-File condition to stop the record reading loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark End of File Flag = Y

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Transaction Category Balance File
acceptance_criteria.When: The file status returned indicates that there are no more records to read (end of file condition, file status = '10')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which will cause the record reading loop to exit after the current iteration completes

rules.rule_name: Final Account Update Triggered at End of File
rules.rule_description: When the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the system must still finalize and save the last account that was being processed, since the account change detection logic only triggers an update when a new account is encountered — meaning the very last account in the file would otherwise never be updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Trigger Final Account Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The End-of-File flag has been set to 'Y', indicating all transaction category balance records have been read, and the last account's interest has been accumulated in the total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The main processing loop detects the End-of-File flag is 'Y' in the ELSE branch of the loop condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account update process (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is invoked for the last account, which adds the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), resets the current cycle credit balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) to zero, resets the current cycle debit balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) to zero, and saves the updated account record back to the Account Master File

rules.rule_name: Detect Account ID Change Between Consecutive Transaction Category Balance Records
rules.rule_description: When processing transaction category balance records sequentially, the program must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the Account ID of the previously processed record. This triggers account-level processing for the new account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account ID on Current Record Matches Previous Account ID?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read, and a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) exists from prior processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is compared against the previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account IDs match, the record belongs to the same account and processing continues directly to the interest rate lookup. If the Account IDs do not match, a new account has been detected and account-level processing is triggered, including optionally updating the prior account, resetting the interest accumulator, and loading data for the new account.

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether a Prior Account Exists Before Triggering Account Update
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected, the program must determine whether this is the very first account encountered during the run. If it is the first account, there is no prior account to update. If a prior account exists, its balance must be finalized before processing the new account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is This the First Record Ever Read?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, meaning the current Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) does not match the previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) to determine if this is the very first account encountered in the current run
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the First-Time Flag is set to 'Y' (first record ever), no prior account update is performed and the First-Time Flag is changed to 'N' to indicate subsequent accounts will require updates. If the First-Time Flag is not 'Y', a prior account exists and the account balance update process is triggered for the previous account before proceeding.

rules.rule_name: Trigger Balance Update for Prior Account When New Account Is Detected
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected and a prior account exists (not the first record), the accumulated interest and cycle reset must be applied to the prior account before processing begins for the new account. This ensures each account's interest is finalized before moving on.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Trigger Account Balance Update for Previous Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is not 'Y', confirming a prior account was being processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The account balance update process (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is invoked for the prior account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) for the prior account is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), the current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero, the current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero, and the updated account record is saved back to the Account Master File.

rules.rule_name: Mark First-Time Processing Flag as Completed on First Account Encounter
rules.rule_description: On the very first account encountered during a program run, the First-Time Processing Flag must be updated to indicate that subsequent account changes will require a prior account balance update. This prevents an erroneous update attempt when no prior account data exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark First-Time Flag as Processed - No Account Update Needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is currently set to 'Y', indicating this is the first account encountered in the run
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the first account change event
acceptance_criteria.Then: The First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', ensuring that all future account changes will correctly trigger a prior account balance update. No account balance update is performed for this first account transition.

rules.rule_name: Reset Running Interest Accumulator When Processing Begins for a New Account
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected, the running total interest accumulator must be reset to zero before processing any transaction category balance records for the new account. This ensures interest is calculated and accumulated independently per account without carrying over values from the prior account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Running Total Interest to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and either the prior account has been updated or this is the first account in the run
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes processing for the new account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is set to zero, ensuring that interest calculations for the new account start from a clean baseline with no carry-over from the previous account.

rules.rule_name: Establish New Account ID as the Current Account Being Processed
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected, the program must record the new Account ID as the current account being tracked. This enables future account change detection by providing the reference Account ID for comparison against subsequent records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set New Account ID as Current Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, the interest accumulator has been reset, and the prior account (if any) has been updated
acceptance_criteria.When: The program establishes the new account as the current account being processed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is stored as the currently tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) for future comparison, and is also set as the key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for retrieving the account's full details from the Account Master File.

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Full Account Details from Account Master File for New Account
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected, the complete account record must be retrieved from the Account Master File. This provides the current balance, account group, and other account attributes required for interest computation and the subsequent account balance update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Full Account Details from Account Master

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected, the current account tracking has been updated, and the Account ID key (FD-ACCT-ID) has been set to the new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program retrieves the account record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account is found, the full account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) is loaded into memory, including the current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), account group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), and cycle credit/debit amounts, making them available for interest rate lookup and balance update. If the account is not found in the Account Master File, a message is displayed indicating the account was not found, identifying the missing Account ID.

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Card Number from Cross-Reference File for New Account
rules.rule_description: When a new account is detected, the card number associated with the account must be retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference File. The card number is required to populate interest transaction records that are written to the Transaction Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Card Number from Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected, the account master record has been successfully retrieved, and the Account ID key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) has been set to the new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program retrieves the card cross-reference record from the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the cross-reference record is found, the card cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is loaded into memory, providing the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) associated with the account, which will be used to populate the card number field on all interest transaction records written for this account. If the account is not found in the Cross-Reference File, a message is displayed indicating the account was not found, identifying the missing Account ID.

rules.rule_name: Detect Account Change in Transaction Category Balance Processing
rules.rule_description: When processing transaction category balance records sequentially, the system must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the Account ID of the record previously processed, signaling that a new account's records are beginning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: New Account ID Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is processing transaction category balance records sequentially, and a current Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is available from the most recently read record, and a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) is held in memory from prior processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record does NOT match the previously tracked Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system recognizes that a new account's records are beginning and triggers the account-change handling workflow, which includes determining whether this is the first account ever encountered, updating the prior account if applicable, resetting the interest accumulator, and loading the new account's data

rules.rule_name: First Account Encountered — Skip Prior Account Update
rules.rule_description: When the very first account is encountered at the start of processing, there is no prior account to update. The system must distinguish this initial state from subsequent account changes to avoid attempting an update on non-existent prior account data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is This the Very First Account Being Processed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is currently set to 'Y', indicating no account has been fully processed yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether this is the very first account being processed by checking if the first-time flag equals 'Y'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines this IS the first account: it skips the prior account balance update step entirely, and instead proceeds directly to mark the first account as processed, reset the interest accumulator, and load the new account's data

rules.rule_name: Mark First Account as Processed to Enable Future Account Updates
rules.rule_description: Once the first account is encountered and recognized as such, the system must update its internal state to indicate that at least one account has now been processed. This ensures that all subsequent account changes will correctly trigger a prior account balance update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark First Account as Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed that the current account is the very first account being processed (first-time flag is 'Y')
acceptance_criteria.When: The first-time account condition is confirmed and the system proceeds to initialize processing for this first account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', so that all future account changes will trigger the prior account balance update rather than skipping it

rules.rule_name: Finalize and Save Prior Account Balance Before Processing New Account
rules.rule_description: Before beginning to process a new account's transaction category balance records, the system must finalize the prior account by applying all accumulated interest to its balance and resetting its cycle-level credit and debit totals, then saving the updated account record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Previous Account Balance

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and this is NOT the first account being processed (first-time flag is 'N'), meaning a prior account's data is held in memory with a fully accumulated interest total (WS-TOTAL-INT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system triggers the prior account update before switching to the new account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the prior account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL); the prior account's current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero; the prior account's current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero; and the updated account record is saved back to the Account Master File

rules.rule_name: Reset Interest Accumulator to Zero for Each New Account
rules.rule_description: Each account must have its interest calculated independently. When processing begins for a new account — whether it is the first account or a subsequent one — the total interest accumulator must be cleared to zero so that interest from a prior account does not carry over into the new account's calculation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Total Interest Accumulator to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and either the prior account has been updated (for subsequent accounts) or the first-time flag has been set to 'N' (for the first account)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes processing for the newly detected account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is set to zero, ensuring that interest calculations for the new account start from a clean baseline with no carry-over from any previously processed account

rules.rule_name: Register New Account ID as the Currently Active Account Being Tracked
rules.rule_description: After the prior account has been finalized and the interest accumulator has been reset, the system must record the new Account ID as the currently active account. This enables future account-change detection by providing a reference point for comparison against subsequent records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Current Account ID as the New Account Being Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The interest accumulator has been reset to zero and the system is ready to begin processing records for the newly detected account, with the new Account ID available from the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system registers the new account as the currently active account being tracked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is stored as the last-known Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) for future account-change comparison, and is also set as the key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for retrieving the account's master record

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account Master Record and Card Cross-Reference for New Account
rules.rule_description: Once a new account is registered as the active account, the system must retrieve two sets of data required for interest calculation and transaction writing: the full account master record (providing balance and account group details) and the card cross-reference record (providing the card number associated with the account).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Retrieve Account Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The new Account ID has been registered as the currently active account (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM and FD-ACCT-ID are set), and the Account Master File and Card Cross-Reference File are open and available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to load all data required for processing the new account's transaction category balance records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account master record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key, loading account details including current balance and account group; AND the system retrieves the card cross-reference record from the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) as the lookup key, loading the card number associated with the account — both records are held in memory for use during interest computation and interest transaction writing for this account

rules.rule_name: Initiate Account Lookup on New Account ID Detection
rules.rule_description: When processing transaction category balance records, a new account lookup must be initiated whenever the account ID on the current record differs from the previously processed account ID. The new account ID is set as the search key to retrieve account details from the Account Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use New Account ID as Search Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been read successfully, and the Account ID on the current record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is different from the last processed Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the account ID change and prepares to retrieve account data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the transaction category balance record is set as the search key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for the Account Master File lookup, and the new Account ID is also saved as the current account being tracked (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account Details from Account Master File
rules.rule_description: When a new account ID is encountered during transaction category balance processing, the system must retrieve the full account record from the Account Master File using the account ID as the direct lookup key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up Account in Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been identified and set as the search key (FD-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a keyed lookup against the Account Master File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Master File is read using the Account ID as the key, and the result is loaded into the account record working area (ACCOUNT-RECORD) for further processing

rules.rule_name: Load Account Details into Memory When Account Record Found
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup is successful, all account attributes are loaded into memory. These attributes — including current balance, current cycle credit and debit amounts, and account group ID — are required for subsequent interest calculation, fee computation, and account balance update steps.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Load Account Details into Memory:
- Current Balance
- Current Cycle Credit Amount
- Current Cycle Debit Amount
- Account Group ID
- Other Account Attributes

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed against the Account Master File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record is found successfully in the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: All account details are loaded into the working account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD), making the following fields available for downstream processing: Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), Current Cycle Credit Amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), Current Cycle Debit Amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), and all other account attributes

rules.rule_name: Display Warning When Account Record Is Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File does not contain a record for the given Account ID, the system must issue a warning message identifying the missing account. Processing continues despite the missing account, but downstream steps such as interest calculation and account update may be incomplete or inaccurate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Warning:
Account Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed against the Account Master File using the Account ID (FD-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching account record is found in the Account Master File for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message is displayed identifying the account that could not be found, in the format: 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' followed by the Account ID that was searched; processing continues without the account data, and downstream processing for this account may be incomplete

rules.rule_name: Set Account ID as Cross-Reference Lookup Key
rules.rule_description: Before searching the Cross-Reference file, the current transaction category balance record's Account ID must be set as the lookup key to identify the correct card cross-reference record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Current Account ID as Lookup Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) has been detected in the transaction category balance record being processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to look up the card cross-reference information for the account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Account ID from the transaction category balance record is assigned as the search key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) to be used for the Cross-Reference file lookup

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Card Cross-Reference Record Using Account ID
rules.rule_description: The Cross-Reference file must be searched using the Account ID as the key to retrieve the card number associated with the account. This card number is required when generating interest transaction records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search Cross-Reference File Using Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID has been set as the lookup key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) and the Cross-Reference file is open for reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs a keyed lookup on the Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference record containing the card number associated with the account is retrieved and stored in the card cross-reference record area (CARD-XREF-RECORD) for subsequent use in interest transaction writing

rules.rule_name: Warn When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: If the Account ID does not exist in the Cross-Reference file, a warning must be displayed identifying the missing account. Processing continues without a valid card number rather than stopping.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Warning: Account Not Found in Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed on the Cross-Reference file using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching record is found in the Cross-Reference file for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' followed by the Account ID is displayed, and processing continues without a valid card number — the program does not stop or abort

rules.rule_name: Store Card Number for Interest Transaction Writing
rules.rule_description: When a valid cross-reference record is found, the card number associated with the account is retained and must be used when writing interest transaction records for that account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Card Number Associated with Account for Use in Interest Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference file lookup was successful and the card cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) has been retrieved containing the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) for the account
acceptance_criteria.When: An interest transaction record is being written for the account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) retrieved from the Cross-Reference file is assigned to the transaction card number field (TRAN-CARD-NUM) on the interest transaction record being written to the Transaction output file

rules.rule_description: The transaction amount for each interest charge record must reflect the exact monthly interest amount computed for that transaction category balance, ensuring the financial value recorded is accurate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Transaction Amount
Monthly Calculated Interest Amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: The monthly interest amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been computed as (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) / 1200 for the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction amount is being assigned to the interest transaction record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount (TRAN-AMT) is set to the computed monthly interest value (WS-MONTHLY-INT)

rules.rule_name: Associate Card Number from Cross-Reference with Interest Transaction
rules.rule_description: Each interest transaction must be linked to the card number associated with the account, retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record that was looked up when the account was first encountered during processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Card Number
From Cross-Reference Lookup

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) has been retrieved for the current account using the Account ID, and the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number is being assigned to the interest transaction record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Card Number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is set to the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup for the account

rules.rule_name: Clear Merchant Details for System-Generated Interest Transactions
rules.rule_description: Since interest charges are system-generated and not associated with any merchant, all merchant-related fields on the interest transaction record must be set to empty or zero values to indicate that no merchant is involved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Merchant Details
Merchant ID = 0
Name / City / Zip = Blank
Not Applicable for Interest Charges

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed for a system-generated interest charge
acceptance_criteria.When: The merchant details are being assigned
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Merchant ID (TRAN-MERCHANT-ID) is set to 0, and the Merchant Name (TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME), Merchant City (TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY), and Merchant ZIP Code (TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP) are all set to blank spaces, indicating no merchant is associated with this interest charge

rules.rule_name: Capture Current System Date and Time for Transaction Timestamping
rules.rule_description: The current system date and time must be captured at the moment the interest transaction is being created, to be used as both the origination and processing timestamps on the transaction record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Capture Current Date and Time
As Transaction Timestamp

acceptance_criteria.Given: An interest transaction record is being prepared for writing to the transaction output file
acceptance_criteria.When: The timestamp is being captured for the transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current system date and time is retrieved and formatted into a standard timestamp format (DB2-FORMAT-TS) containing year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds components, ready to be applied to the transaction record

rules.rule_name: Stamp Interest Transaction with Origination and Processing Timestamps
rules.rule_description: Both the origination timestamp and the processing timestamp on the interest transaction record must be set to the same current date-time value, reflecting that the transaction was both originated and processed at the same point in time by the system.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Transaction Timestamps
Origination Timestamp = Current Date-Time
Processing Timestamp = Current Date-Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date and time has been captured and formatted into the standard timestamp (DB2-FORMAT-TS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The timestamps are being assigned to the interest transaction record
acceptance_criteria.Then: Both the Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) and the Transaction Processing Timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS) are set to the same current formatted timestamp value (DB2-FORMAT-TS), indicating the transaction was originated and processed at the same time

rules.rule_name: Write Completed Interest Transaction Record to Output File
rules.rule_description: Once all fields of the interest transaction record have been populated, the complete record must be written to the Transaction Output File to permanently record the interest charge.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Transaction Record
To Transaction Output File

acceptance_criteria.Given: All fields of the interest transaction record (TRAN-RECORD) have been fully populated including transaction ID, type, category, source, description, amount, card number, merchant details, and timestamps
acceptance_criteria.When: The completed interest transaction record is submitted for writing to the Transaction Output File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction record (FD-TRANFILE-REC) is successfully written to the Transaction Output File, and the transaction is permanently recorded as an interest charge for the account

rules.rule_name: Increment Transaction Sequence Counter Before ID Generation
rules.rule_description: Each time an interest transaction is to be recorded, the system increments a running sequence counter by 1 to ensure each transaction receives a unique sequential number within the processing run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Sequence Counter by 1 e.g. 00001 → 00002

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to generate a unique Transaction ID for a new interest transaction record, and a running sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) holds the value from the previously generated transaction (or zero if this is the first transaction in the run)
acceptance_criteria.When: A new interest transaction is ready to be written to the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) must be incremented by exactly 1 before the Transaction ID is formed, so that each transaction in the same processing run receives a strictly increasing, unique numeric suffix

rules.rule_name: Combine Processing Date and Sequence Number to Form Unique Transaction ID
rules.rule_description: The unique Transaction ID is constructed by concatenating the Processing Date parameter (passed into the program at runtime) with the incremented sequence counter, forming a single composite identifier that is unique within the processing run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Combine Two Parts into Transaction ID: Processing Date + Sequence Number e.g. 20241215 + 00002 = '2024121500002'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Processing Date parameter (PARM-DATE) has been provided to the program at runtime representing the date of the processing run, and the sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) has just been incremented by 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system constructs the Transaction ID for the current interest transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) must be formed by concatenating the full Processing Date (PARM-DATE) immediately followed by the current sequence counter value (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), with both values used at their full defined sizes without truncation or delimiter separation, resulting in a composite identifier such as '2024121500002'

rules.rule_name: Store Generated Transaction ID in the Interest Transaction Record
rules.rule_description: Once the unique Transaction ID has been generated, it is stored in the Transaction Record field (TRAN-ID) so that it is available as part of the complete transaction record that will be written to the Transaction Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Generated Unique Transaction ID for use in Transaction Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A unique Transaction ID has been successfully generated by combining the Processing Date and the incremented sequence counter into TRAN-ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates all fields of the interest Transaction Record prior to writing it to the Transaction Output File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The generated Transaction ID value stored in TRAN-ID must be included as part of the Transaction Record (TRAN-RECORD) that is written to the Transaction Output File, ensuring the transaction is permanently recorded with its unique identifier

rules.rule_name: Fee Computation Reserved for Future Implementation
rules.rule_description: This rule defines the fee calculation step as a placeholder process that is invoked after interest computation for a transaction category balance record where a non-zero interest rate exists. rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Fee Computation
Not Yet Implemented
Reserved for Future Use

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been processed, a non-zero interest rate was found for the account group, transaction category code, and transaction type code combination, and the monthly interest has already been computed and accumulated for the current account
acceptance_criteria.When: The fee computation step is invoked as the next action following interest calculation for the current transaction category balance record
acceptance_criteria.Then: No fee calculation is performed and no fee transaction record is written; the process completes without any changes to account balances, transaction records, or any other business data, and control returns to the main processing loop to continue with the next transaction category balance record

rules.rule_name: Add Total Calculated Interest to Account Current Balance
rules.rule_description: When an account balance update is triggered, the total interest accumulated across all transaction categories for the account during the current cycle is added to the account's existing current balance to produce the new updated balance.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Add Total Calculated Interest
to Account Current Balance

New Balance = Current Balance + Total Interest

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered either because a new account ID was detected in the transaction category balance file or the end of the transaction category balance file has been reached, AND the total interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT) has been accumulated across all transaction category balance records processed for the current account
acceptance_criteria.When: The account balance update process is executed for the current account
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) must be increased by the total accumulated interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT), resulting in a new current balance equal to the prior current balance plus the total interest calculated for the account

rules.rule_name: Reset Current Cycle Credit Amount to Zero
rules.rule_description: As part of the end-of-cycle account update, the current cycle credit amount on the account record is cleared to zero, signifying that the credit activity for the current billing cycle has been fully processed and the cycle is being closed out.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Current Cycle
Credit Amount to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered for the current account, AND the total interest has already been added to the account's current balance
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record is being prepared for saving back to the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) on the account record must be set to zero, indicating that all credit activity for the current cycle has been processed and the cycle credit balance is cleared

rules.rule_name: Reset Current Cycle Debit Amount to Zero
rules.rule_description: As part of the end-of-cycle account update, the current cycle debit amount on the account record is cleared to zero, signifying that the debit activity for the current billing cycle has been fully processed and the cycle is being closed out.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Current Cycle
Debit Amount to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered for the current account, AND the total interest has been added to the account's current balance, AND the current cycle credit amount has already been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record is being prepared for saving back to the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) on the account record must be set to zero, indicating that all debit activity for the current cycle has been processed and the cycle debit balance is cleared

rules.rule_name: Save Updated Account Record to Account Master File
rules.rule_description: After the account's current balance has been updated with total interest and the current cycle credit and debit amounts have been reset to zero, the updated account record must be persisted back to the Account Master File to make the changes permanent.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Updated Account Record
to Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account record has been updated with the new current balance (original balance plus total interest), the current cycle credit amount has been set to zero, and the current cycle debit amount has been set to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record update is written back to the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete updated account record must be saved to the Account Master File, replacing the existing account record for that account ID, so that the new balance and cleared cycle amounts are permanently recorded

rules.rule_name: Validate Account Record Successfully Updated in Account Master File
rules.rule_description: After attempting to save the updated account record to the Account Master File, the outcome of the save operation must be validated. If the save was not successful, the program must stop processing immediately to prevent data inconsistency, as the account balance update is a critical operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Account Record
Successfully Updated?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to save the updated account record (with new balance and zeroed cycle amounts) back to the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The result of the account record save operation is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account record was saved successfully, processing continues to the next step; If the account record was NOT saved successfully, an error message 'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE' is displayed and the program immediately stops all processing, as continuing with an unrecorded account balance update would result in data integrity issues

rules.rule_name: Trigger Account Balance Update on New Account Detection
rules.rule_description: The account balance update process must be triggered at the correct point in processing — either when a new account ID is encountered in the transaction category balance file (indicating all records for the prior account have been read) or when the end of the transaction category balance file is reached (ensuring the last account is also updated).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Account Balance Update Triggered
New Account Detected or End of File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is processing transaction category balance records sequentially, AND at least one account has been fully processed (i.e., this is not the very first account encountered in the file)
acceptance_criteria.When: Either (a) the Account ID on the current transaction category balance record is different from the Account ID of the previously processed record, indicating a new account group has started, OR (b) the end of the transaction category balance file has been reached, indicating the last account's records have all been read
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account balance update process must be invoked for the account that was just completed, applying the total accumulated interest to its balance and resetting its cycle credit and debit amounts to zero before beginning processing for the new account or before closing the program

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

    EOF([End of Transaction Category\nBalance File Reached])

rules.rule_name: Trigger Final Account Update Upon End of Transaction Category Balance File
rules.rule_description: When the end of the Transaction Category Balance file is reached, the program must determine whether at least one account was processed during the run. If at least one account was processed, the final account's accumulated data must be updated. If no accounts were processed (file was empty), no update action is taken and processing proceeds directly to closing all files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was at Least One Account Processed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been reading Transaction Category Balance records sequentially and has now reached the end of the Transaction Category Balance file, and the end-of-file condition is set to 'Y'
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected within the main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: If at least one account was previously processed during this run (i.e., the first-time processing flag was set to 'N', meaning at least one account record was encountered), the final account update procedure must be invoked to finalize that account's data; if no accounts were processed (file was empty and first-time flag remains 'Y'), no account update is performed and processing proceeds directly to closing all files

rules.rule_name: Apply Total Accumulated Interest to Account Current Balance
rules.rule_description: As part of the final account update, the total interest amount accumulated across all transaction category balance records for the last processed account must be added to that account's current balance in the Account Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Total Accumulated Interest to Account Current Balance

acceptance_criteria.Given: The final account update has been triggered for the last processed account, and the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) has been computed by summing monthly interest charges across all transaction categories and transaction types for that account
acceptance_criteria.When: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), increasing the balance by the full interest amount owed for the current cycle

rules.rule_name: Reset Current Cycle Credit Amount to Zero on Account Update
rules.rule_description: As part of the final account update, the current billing cycle's total credit amount for the account must be reset to zero, signifying that the cycle's credit activity has been fully processed and the account is ready for the next billing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Current Cycle Credit Amount to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is being executed for the last processed account, and the total accumulated interest has already been applied to the account's current balance
acceptance_criteria.When: The current cycle credit reset step is performed within the account update procedure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account's current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is set to zero, clearing all credit activity recorded for the current billing cycle

rules.rule_name: Reset Current Cycle Debit Amount to Zero on Account Update
rules.rule_description: As part of the final account update, the current billing cycle's total debit amount for the account must be reset to zero, signifying that the cycle's debit activity has been fully processed and the account is ready for the next billing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Current Cycle Debit Amount to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is being executed for the last processed account, and both the interest has been applied to the current balance and the current cycle credit amount has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The current cycle debit reset step is performed within the account update procedure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account's current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is set to zero, clearing all debit activity recorded for the current billing cycle

rules.rule_name: Persist Updated Account Record to Account Master File
rules.rule_description: After applying the accumulated interest to the current balance and resetting the current cycle credit and debit amounts, the updated account record must be saved back to the Account Master File to make the changes permanent.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Updated Account Record to Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) has completed applying total accumulated interest to the current balance and has reset both the current cycle credit amount and current cycle debit amount to zero for the last processed account
acceptance_criteria.When: The save step is executed to persist the updated account data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The updated account record — containing the new current balance (with interest applied), zero current cycle credit amount, and zero current cycle debit amount — is written back to the Account Master File by rewriting the existing account record; if the save is successful, processing proceeds to close all files; if the save fails, an account file write error is reported and the program terminates abnormally

rules.rule_name: Program Completion Announcement
rules.rule_description: Upon successful completion of all processing, the program announces its end of execution before closing any files, providing an audit trail of program lifecycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C'

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records have been fully processed and the last account update has been applied
acceptance_criteria.When: The program has finished its main processing loop and is ready to shut down
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C' to signal successful completion of all business processing before any file closure begins

rules.rule_name: Close Transaction Category Balance File on Program Completion
