rules.rule_description: The Transaction Category Balance input file must be properly closed as the first file closure step during program completion to ensure data integrity and release file resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Transaction Category Balance File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has displayed its end-of-execution message and is proceeding with the shutdown sequence
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Transaction Category Balance file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Balance file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION BALANCE FILE' error and terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Close Cross-Reference File on Program Completion
rules.rule_description: The Card Cross-Reference input file must be properly closed as the second file closure step during program completion, following the closure of the Transaction Category Balance file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING CROSS REF FILE' error and terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Close Disclosure Group File on Program Completion
rules.rule_description: The Disclosure Group input file, which holds interest rate data, must be properly closed as the third file closure step during program completion, following the closure of the Cross-Reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Disclosure Group File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference file has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Disclosure Group file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Disclosure Group file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' error and terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Close Account Master File on Program Completion
rules.rule_description: The Account Master file, which was opened for both reading and updating, must be properly closed as the fourth file closure step during program completion to ensure all account balance updates are committed and the file is properly released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group file has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Account Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Master file must be successfully closed, ensuring all account balance updates and cycle resets written during processing are preserved; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' error and terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Close Transaction Output File on Program Completion
rules.rule_description: The Transaction output file, which holds all newly generated interest transaction records, must be properly closed as the fifth and final file closure step during program completion to ensure all written interest transactions are committed and available for downstream processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Transaction Output File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master file has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Transaction output file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction output file must be successfully closed, ensuring all interest transaction records written during processing are preserved and available; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION FILE' error and terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Mandatory Sequential File Closure Order
rules.rule_description: All five files used by the program must be closed in a strict mandatory sequence during program completion: Transaction Category Balance → Cross-Reference → Disclosure Group → Account Master → Transaction Output. This sequence ensures orderly shutdown and data integrity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Program Completion Triggered

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed all transaction category balance record processing including the final account update
acceptance_criteria.When: The program enters its completion phase
acceptance_criteria.Then: All five files must be closed in the following strict order: (1) Transaction Category Balance file, (2) Cross-Reference file, (3) Disclosure Group file, (4) Account Master file, (5) Transaction Output file; each file must be successfully closed before the next closure is attempted; if any file closure fails, the program must report the specific file error and terminate abnormally without proceeding to close remaining files

rules.rule_name: Program Successful Termination
rules.rule_description: After all files have been successfully closed, the program must return control to the calling environment, signaling successful and complete execution of all interest calculation and account update business processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Program Successfully Ended

acceptance_criteria.Given: All five files — Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, and Transaction Output — have been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program has completed all shutdown steps
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must return control to the calling environment (GOBACK), indicating that all interest calculations, account balance updates, cycle credit and debit resets, and interest transaction record writes have been completed successfully

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C is starting execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Category Balance File, Cross-Reference File, Disclosure Group File, Account Master File, and Transaction Output File in sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All five files must be successfully opened before any record processing begins; the Transaction Category Balance File and Cross-Reference File and Disclosure Group File are opened for input only, the Account Master File is opened for both reading and updating, and the Transaction Output File is opened for writing new records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization - Open All Required Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any processing begins, the program must successfully open all five required files: Transaction Category Balance (input), Cross-Reference (input), Disclosure Group (input), Account Master (input/output), and Transaction Output (output). Processing cannot proceed if any file fails to open.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance File has been successfully opened and the program is in its main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Transaction Category Balance File sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a record is successfully read, the record count is incremented by 1 and the record is displayed, and processing continues with account change detection; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set to 'Y' and the final account update is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Transaction Category Balance Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads transaction category balance records one at a time in sequential order from the Transaction Category Balance File. Each record contains an Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, and a balance amount that will be used for interest calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read and the program has a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is compared to the last processed Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account IDs are different, an account change is detected and the program must finalize the prior account before initializing for the new account; if the Account IDs are the same, the program proceeds directly to interest rate lookup for the current record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Change Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: Since transaction category balance records are grouped by Account ID, the program must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the previously processed Account ID. This signals that all records for the prior account have been processed and a new account's records are beginning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account change has been detected on the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-FIRST-TIME is 'Y' (this is the first account encountered), the prior account update is skipped and WS-FIRST-TIME is set to 'N'; if WS-FIRST-TIME is 'N' (a prior account exists), the prior account balance update is performed before processing the new account

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Record Processed Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account change is detected, the program must determine whether this is the very first account being processed. On the first account, there is no prior account to update, so the account update step must be skipped. The first-time flag is initialized to 'Y' and set to 'N' after the first account is encountered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account change has been detected and either the prior account has been updated or this is the first account being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes processing for the new account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is reset to zero, the new Account ID is saved as the current Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM), and the Account ID is set as the key for subsequent Account Master and Cross-Reference file lookups

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Interest Accumulation Reset for New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing begins for a new account, the total interest accumulator must be reset to zero to ensure that interest calculated for the new account is not contaminated by interest amounts from the previously processed account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been identified from the transaction category balance record and the Account Master File is open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Account Master File using the Account ID (FD-ACCT-ID) as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account is found, the full account record including current balance, account group ID, current cycle credits, and current cycle debits is loaded into memory for use in subsequent processing; if the account is not found, a message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: [Account ID]' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is encountered, the program retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key. The account record provides the current balance, account group ID, and cycle credit/debit amounts needed for interest application and account update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master record has been retrieved for the new account and the Cross-Reference File is open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the cross-reference record is found, the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) associated with the account is loaded into memory for use when writing interest transaction records; if the account is not found in the cross-reference file, a message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: [Account ID]' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Cross-Reference Lookup for Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is encountered, the program retrieves the card cross-reference record using the Account ID as the lookup key. The cross-reference record provides the Card Number associated with the account, which is required as a field on every interest transaction record written to the output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master record has been retrieved providing the Account Group ID, and the current transaction category balance record provides the Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Disclosure Group File using the composite key of Account Group ID (FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID) + Transaction Category Code (FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD) + Transaction Type Code (FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching disclosure group record is found, the interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) from that record is used for interest calculation; if no matching record is found, the program falls back to the default interest rate lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Interest Rate Lookup by Account Group, Transaction Category, and Transaction Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction category balance record, the applicable annual interest rate is looked up from the Disclosure Group File using a composite key of Account Group ID, Transaction Category Code, and Transaction Type Code. This determines the rate to apply to the specific balance category for the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group File lookup using the specific Account Group ID returned no matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retries the Disclosure Group File lookup with the Account Group ID overridden to 'DEFAULT' while retaining the original Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate from the DEFAULT disclosure group record is used for the interest calculation for this transaction category balance record; if the DEFAULT record is also not found, a processing error is raised

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Interest Rate Fallback When Specific Rate Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no interest rate record exists for the specific Account Group, Transaction Category, and Transaction Type combination, the program retries the lookup using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID while keeping the same Transaction Category Code and Transaction Type Code. This ensures a fallback rate is always available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest rate has been retrieved from the Disclosure Group File for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether the retrieved interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the interest rate is zero, both the interest calculation and the fee calculation are skipped entirely and the program reads the next transaction category balance record; if the interest rate is greater than zero, the program proceeds to calculate monthly interest

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zero Interest Rate Skip Rule
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the interest rate retrieved from the Disclosure Group File (either specific or default) is zero, no interest calculation and no fee calculation is performed for that transaction category balance record. The program skips directly to reading the next record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A non-zero interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) has been retrieved and the transaction category balance (TRAN-CAT-BAL) is available from the current record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program computes the monthly interest for the transaction category
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Monthly Interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT) is calculated as: (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) divided by 1200

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Interest Calculation Formula
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a non-zero interest rate exists, the monthly interest charge for a transaction category balance is calculated by multiplying the category balance by the annual interest rate and dividing by 1200. Dividing by 1200 converts the annual percentage rate to a monthly decimal rate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Monthly interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been calculated for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program adds the monthly interest to the account-level interest accumulator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is increased by the computed monthly interest amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT), representing the cumulative interest across all processed transaction categories for the current account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Total Interest Accumulation Across Transaction Categories
all_rules.Rule_Description: The monthly interest calculated for each transaction category balance record is added to a running total for the current account. This accumulates interest across all transaction categories and transaction types belonging to the same account before the account balance is updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Monthly interest has been calculated and the Transaction ID has been generated for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program creates and writes an interest transaction record to the Transaction Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record is written with: Transaction ID set to the generated ID, Transaction Type Code set to '01', Transaction Category Code set to '05', Transaction Source set to 'System', Transaction Description set to 'Int. for a/c ' concatenated with the Account ID, Transaction Amount set to the computed monthly interest (WS-MONTHLY-INT), Merchant ID set to zero, Merchant Name left blank, Merchant City left blank, Merchant ZIP left blank, Card Number set to the card number retrieved from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM), Original Timestamp set to the current system timestamp, and Processing Timestamp set to the current system timestamp

all_rules.Rule_Name: Interest Transaction Record Creation
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every transaction category balance where interest is computed, a system-generated interest transaction record is written to the Transaction Output File. The record captures the interest charge with standardized codes identifying it as a system-generated interest transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest transaction is about to be written to the Transaction Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program generates the Transaction ID for the interest transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is formed by concatenating the processing date parameter (PARM-DATE) with the current value of the transaction suffix counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), where WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is incremented by 1 before each transaction is written, ensuring each transaction receives a unique identifier

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction ID Generation for Interest Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each interest transaction written to the output file must have a unique Transaction ID. The ID is constructed by combining a processing date parameter with an auto-incrementing numeric suffix that increases by one for each transaction written during the program run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Monthly interest has been calculated and the interest transaction record has been written for a transaction category balance record with a non-zero interest rate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the fee calculation step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No fee calculation is performed at this time as the fee logic is not yet implemented; the program proceeds to read the next transaction category balance record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fee Calculation Placeholder
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program includes a fee calculation step that is invoked after interest is computed for any transaction category balance record with a non-zero interest rate. However, the fee calculation logic has not yet been implemented and currently performs no action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records for the current account have been processed and the total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) holds the sum of all monthly interest amounts for that account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program finalizes processing for the account and updates the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) is increased by the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT); the current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is set to zero; the current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is set to zero; and the updated account record is written back to the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Balance Update - Apply Accumulated Interest and Reset Cycle Amounts
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transaction category balance records for an account have been processed, the account's current balance is increased by the total accumulated interest for that account, and the current cycle credit and debit amounts are both reset to zero. The updated account record is then saved back to the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end of the Transaction Category Balance File has been reached and the last account's transaction category balance records have all been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected in the main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account balance update is performed for the last account: the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), the current cycle credit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero, the current cycle debit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero, and the updated account record is saved to the Account Master File before the program proceeds to close all files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Final Account Update at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the Transaction Category Balance File is reached, the last account being processed must still receive its balance update. Since the account update is normally triggered by detecting a new account on the next record, a special end-of-file handler ensures the final account is not skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records have been processed and the final account balance has been updated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes its main processing loop and proceeds to termination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Balance File is closed, followed by the Cross-Reference File, then the Disclosure Group File, then the Account Master File, and finally the Transaction Output File; after all files are successfully closed, the program terminates normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion - Close All Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of all record processing, the program must close all five files in sequence: Transaction Category Balance File, Cross-Reference File, Disclosure Group File, Account Master File, and Transaction Output File. All files must be properly closed before the program terminates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The interest calculation program CBACT04C is invoked by the batch scheduler or operator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C' to confirm the program has started, before any file is opened or any data is processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Execution Start Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The interest calculation program CBACT04C must announce its start before any file operations or processing begins, providing an audit trail of program execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C has started execution and is in the initialization phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Category Balance file for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Cross-Reference file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION CATEGORY BALANCE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction Category Balance File for Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Category Balance file, which contains the balance amounts per transaction category and type for each account, must be successfully opened in read-only mode before interest calculation processing can begin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file has been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Cross-Reference file for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Disclosure Group file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE' along with the file status value, records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Cross-Reference File for Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cross-Reference file, which maps Account IDs to Card Numbers and is required for populating interest transaction records, must be successfully opened in read-only mode as part of program initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file and Cross-Reference file have been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Disclosure Group file for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Account Master file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Disclosure Group File for Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Disclosure Group file, which contains the interest rates applicable per account group, transaction category, and transaction type, must be successfully opened in read-only mode as part of program initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, and Disclosure Group files have been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Master file for both reading and updating
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully in read-update mode, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Transaction Output file); if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT MASTER FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account Master File for Reading and Updating
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master file must be opened in both read and update mode (not read-only) because the program must both retrieve current account balances and write back updated balances after interest is applied. This dual-access mode is a critical business requirement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, and Account Master files have all been successfully opened and the program is completing initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Output file for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to the main interest calculation processing loop; if the file fails to open, the program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further processing is allowed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction Output File for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Output file, which will receive newly generated interest transaction records created during processing, must be successfully opened in write-only mode as the final step of program initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C has started execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs its initialization phase
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The files must be opened in the following strict sequence: (1) Transaction Category Balance file for reading, (2) Cross-Reference file for reading, (3) Disclosure Group file for reading, (4) Account Master file for reading and updating, (5) Transaction Output file for writing; each file must open successfully before the next is attempted; if any file fails to open, the program terminates immediately without attempting to open subsequent files; only after all five files are successfully opened does the program proceed to interest calculation processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mandatory Sequential File Opening Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: All five required files must be opened in a strict, mandatory sequence during program initialization. Each file must be successfully opened before the next file opening is attempted. Interest calculation processing may only begin after all five files are confirmed open and ready.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program CBACT04C is initializing for an interest calculation run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one of the five required files — Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, or Transaction Output — cannot be successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must not proceed to interest calculation processing under any circumstances; the program must display a descriptive error message identifying which file failed to open, display the diagnostic file status information, and terminate abnormally; this policy ensures no partial interest calculations are performed with incomplete data sources

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Files Must Be Available Before Processing Begins
all_rules.Rule_Description: Interest calculation processing is a dependent workflow — it requires all five data sources and output destinations to be available simultaneously. If any single file is unavailable, the entire interest calculation run must be aborted to prevent partial or inconsistent results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance File has been successfully opened and the End-of-File flag is set to 'N' (not yet reached end of file)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next available transaction category balance record from the Transaction Category Balance File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next transaction category balance record is retrieved and loaded into the transaction category balance record buffer, making its data (Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Balance) available for subsequent interest calculation processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Transaction Category Balance Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads transaction category balance records one at a time, sequentially from the Transaction Category Balance File, to drive the interest calculation process for each account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Transaction Category Balance File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read was successful (file status = '00'), the record is considered valid and processing continues with incrementing the record counter and displaying the record; if the end of file has been reached (file status = '10'), the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y' and the final account update is triggered; if any other file status is returned, the read is treated as a file read error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Record Read Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each read attempt from the Transaction Category Balance File, the system determines whether a valid record was retrieved or whether the end of the file has been reached, directing the program flow accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read from the Transaction Category Balance File (End-of-File flag remains 'N')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the record was read without error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record counter (WS-RECORD-COUNT) is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly processed record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Counter Increment on Successful Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time a valid transaction category balance record is successfully read, the program increments a running counter to track the total number of records processed during the execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read and the record counter has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds with processing the record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete transaction category balance record content (including Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Balance amount) is displayed as part of the processing audit trail

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display of Transaction Category Balance Record Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a valid transaction category balance record is read and counted, the full content of the record is displayed to provide an audit trail of all records being processed during program execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read, the record counter has been incremented, and the record details have been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the record reading and logging steps
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction category balance record data (Account ID, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Balance) is made available to the interest calculation processing stage, which evaluates account changes, retrieves account and cross-reference data, looks up interest rates, and computes interest charges

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pass Valid Record to Interest Calculation Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction category balance record has been read, counted, and displayed, it is passed forward to the interest calculation processing stage where account data is retrieved and interest is computed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Transaction Category Balance File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status returned indicates that there are no more records to read (end of file condition, file status = '10')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which will cause the record reading loop to exit after the current iteration completes

all_rules.Rule_Name: End of File Detection and Flag Setting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no more transaction category balance records are available in the file, the system marks the End-of-File condition to stop the record reading loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The End-of-File flag has been set to 'Y', indicating all transaction category balance records have been read, and the last account's interest has been accumulated in the total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main processing loop detects the End-of-File flag is 'Y' in the ELSE branch of the loop condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account update process (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is invoked for the last account, which adds the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), resets the current cycle credit balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) to zero, resets the current cycle debit balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) to zero, and saves the updated account record back to the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Final Account Update Triggered at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the system must still finalize and save the last account that was being processed, since the account change detection logic only triggers an update when a new account is encountered — meaning the very last account in the file would otherwise never be updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been successfully read, and a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) exists from prior processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is compared against the previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account IDs match, the record belongs to the same account and processing continues directly to the interest rate lookup. If the Account IDs do not match, a new account has been detected and account-level processing is triggered, including optionally updating the prior account, resetting the interest accumulator, and loading data for the new account.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Account ID Change Between Consecutive Transaction Category Balance Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing transaction category balance records sequentially, the program must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the Account ID of the previously processed record. This triggers account-level processing for the new account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, meaning the current Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) does not match the previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) to determine if this is the very first account encountered in the current run
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the First-Time Flag is set to 'Y' (first record ever), no prior account update is performed and the First-Time Flag is changed to 'N' to indicate subsequent accounts will require updates. If the First-Time Flag is not 'Y', a prior account exists and the account balance update process is triggered for the previous account before proceeding.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether a Prior Account Exists Before Triggering Account Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected, the program must determine whether this is the very first account encountered during the run. If it is the first account, there is no prior account to update. If a prior account exists, its balance must be finalized before processing the new account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is not 'Y', confirming a prior account was being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account balance update process (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is invoked for the prior account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) for the prior account is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), the current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero, the current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero, and the updated account record is saved back to the Account Master File.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Balance Update for Prior Account When New Account Is Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected and a prior account exists (not the first record), the accumulated interest and cycle reset must be applied to the prior account before processing begins for the new account. This ensures each account's interest is finalized before moving on.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is currently set to 'Y', indicating this is the first account encountered in the run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the first account change event
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First-Time Processing Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', ensuring that all future account changes will correctly trigger a prior account balance update. No account balance update is performed for this first account transition.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark First-Time Processing Flag as Completed on First Account Encounter
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the very first account encountered during a program run, the First-Time Processing Flag must be updated to indicate that subsequent account changes will require a prior account balance update. This prevents an erroneous update attempt when no prior account data exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and either the prior account has been updated or this is the first account in the run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes processing for the new account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is set to zero, ensuring that interest calculations for the new account start from a clean baseline with no carry-over from the previous account.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Running Interest Accumulator When Processing Begins for a New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected, the running total interest accumulator must be reset to zero before processing any transaction category balance records for the new account. This ensures interest is calculated and accumulated independently per account without carrying over values from the prior account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, the interest accumulator has been reset, and the prior account (if any) has been updated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program establishes the new account as the current account being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is stored as the currently tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) for future comparison, and is also set as the key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for retrieving the account's full details from the Account Master File.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Establish New Account ID as the Current Account Being Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected, the program must record the new Account ID as the current account being tracked. This enables future account change detection by providing the reference Account ID for comparison against subsequent records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected, the current account tracking has been updated, and the Account ID key (FD-ACCT-ID) has been set to the new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retrieves the account record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account is found, the full account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) is loaded into memory, including the current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), account group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), and cycle credit/debit amounts, making them available for interest rate lookup and balance update. If the account is not found in the Account Master File, a message is displayed indicating the account was not found, identifying the missing Account ID.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Full Account Details from Account Master File for New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected, the complete account record must be retrieved from the Account Master File. This provides the current balance, account group, and other account attributes required for interest computation and the subsequent account balance update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new account ID has been detected, the account master record has been successfully retrieved, and the Account ID key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) has been set to the new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retrieves the card cross-reference record from the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the cross-reference record is found, the card cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is loaded into memory, providing the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) associated with the account, which will be used to populate the card number field on all interest transaction records written for this account. If the account is not found in the Cross-Reference File, a message is displayed indicating the account was not found, identifying the missing Account ID.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Card Number from Cross-Reference File for New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is detected, the card number associated with the account must be retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference File. The card number is required to populate interest transaction records that are written to the Transaction Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing transaction category balance records sequentially, and a current Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is available from the most recently read record, and a previously tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) is held in memory from prior processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID on the current transaction category balance record does NOT match the previously tracked Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system recognizes that a new account's records are beginning and triggers the account-change handling workflow, which includes determining whether this is the first account ever encountered, updating the prior account if applicable, resetting the interest accumulator, and loading the new account's data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Account Change in Transaction Category Balance Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing transaction category balance records sequentially, the system must detect when the Account ID on the current record differs from the Account ID of the record previously processed, signaling that a new account's records are beginning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is currently set to 'Y', indicating no account has been fully processed yet
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether this is the very first account being processed by checking if the first-time flag equals 'Y'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines this IS the first account: it skips the prior account balance update step entirely, and instead proceeds directly to mark the first account as processed, reset the interest accumulator, and load the new account's data

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Account Encountered — Skip Prior Account Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the very first account is encountered at the start of processing, there is no prior account to update. The system must distinguish this initial state from subsequent account changes to avoid attempting an update on non-existent prior account data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed that the current account is the very first account being processed (first-time flag is 'Y')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first-time account condition is confirmed and the system proceeds to initialize processing for this first account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', so that all future account changes will trigger the prior account balance update rather than skipping it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark First Account as Processed to Enable Future Account Updates
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the first account is encountered and recognized as such, the system must update its internal state to indicate that at least one account has now been processed. This ensures that all subsequent account changes will correctly trigger a prior account balance update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and this is NOT the first account being processed (first-time flag is 'N'), meaning a prior account's data is held in memory with a fully accumulated interest total (WS-TOTAL-INT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system triggers the prior account update before switching to the new account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the prior account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL); the prior account's current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is reset to zero; the prior account's current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is reset to zero; and the updated account record is saved back to the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Finalize and Save Prior Account Balance Before Processing New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before beginning to process a new account's transaction category balance records, the system must finalize the prior account by applying all accumulated interest to its balance and resetting its cycle-level credit and debit totals, then saving the updated account record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been detected on the current transaction category balance record, and either the prior account has been updated (for subsequent accounts) or the first-time flag has been set to 'N' (for the first account)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes processing for the newly detected account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is set to zero, ensuring that interest calculations for the new account start from a clean baseline with no carry-over from any previously processed account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Interest Accumulator to Zero for Each New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each account must have its interest calculated independently. When processing begins for a new account — whether it is the first account or a subsequent one — the total interest accumulator must be cleared to zero so that interest from a prior account does not carry over into the new account's calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The interest accumulator has been reset to zero and the system is ready to begin processing records for the newly detected account, with the new Account ID available from the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system registers the new account as the currently active account being tracked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the current transaction category balance record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is stored as the last-known Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM) for future account-change comparison, and is also set as the key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for retrieving the account's master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Register New Account ID as the Currently Active Account Being Tracked
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the prior account has been finalized and the interest accumulator has been reset, the system must record the new Account ID as the currently active account. This enables future account-change detection by providing a reference point for comparison against subsequent records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The new Account ID has been registered as the currently active account (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM and FD-ACCT-ID are set), and the Account Master File and Card Cross-Reference File are open and available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to load all data required for processing the new account's transaction category balance records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account master record from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key, loading account details including current balance and account group; AND the system retrieves the card cross-reference record from the Cross-Reference File using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) as the lookup key, loading the card number associated with the account — both records are held in memory for use during interest computation and interest transaction writing for this account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Master Record and Card Cross-Reference for New Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a new account is registered as the active account, the system must retrieve two sets of data required for interest calculation and transaction writing: the full account master record (providing balance and account group details) and the card cross-reference record (providing the card number associated with the account).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been read successfully, and the Account ID on the current record (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) is different from the last processed Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the account ID change and prepares to retrieve account data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Account ID from the transaction category balance record is set as the search key (FD-ACCT-ID) to be used for the Account Master File lookup, and the new Account ID is also saved as the current account being tracked (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Account Lookup on New Account ID Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing transaction category balance records, a new account lookup must be initiated whenever the account ID on the current record differs from the previously processed account ID. The new account ID is set as the search key to retrieve account details from the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID has been identified and set as the search key (FD-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a keyed lookup against the Account Master File using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File is read using the Account ID as the key, and the result is loaded into the account record working area (ACCOUNT-RECORD) for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Details from Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account ID is encountered during transaction category balance processing, the system must retrieve the full account record from the Account Master File using the account ID as the direct lookup key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed against the Account Master File using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is found successfully in the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All account details are loaded into the working account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD), making the following fields available for downstream processing: Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), Current Cycle Credit Amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), Current Cycle Debit Amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), and all other account attributes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Account Details into Memory When Account Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup is successful, all account attributes are loaded into memory. These attributes — including current balance, current cycle credit and debit amounts, and account group ID — are required for subsequent interest calculation, fee computation, and account balance update steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed against the Account Master File using the Account ID (FD-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching account record is found in the Account Master File for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A warning message is displayed identifying the account that could not be found, in the format: 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' followed by the Account ID that was searched; processing continues without the account data, and downstream processing for this account may be incomplete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Warning When Account Record Is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File does not contain a record for the given Account ID, the system must issue a warning message identifying the missing account. Processing continues despite the missing account, but downstream steps such as interest calculation and account update may be incomplete or inaccurate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Account ID (TRANCAT-ACCT-ID) has been detected in the transaction category balance record being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to look up the card cross-reference information for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Account ID from the transaction category balance record is assigned as the search key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) to be used for the Cross-Reference file lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Account ID as Cross-Reference Lookup Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before searching the Cross-Reference file, the current transaction category balance record's Account ID must be set as the lookup key to identify the correct card cross-reference record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been set as the lookup key (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID) and the Cross-Reference file is open for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs a keyed lookup on the Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference record containing the card number associated with the account is retrieved and stored in the card cross-reference record area (CARD-XREF-RECORD) for subsequent use in interest transaction writing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Card Cross-Reference Record Using Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cross-Reference file must be searched using the Account ID as the key to retrieve the card number associated with the account. This card number is required when generating interest transaction records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed on the Cross-Reference file using the Account ID (FD-XREF-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching record is found in the Cross-Reference file for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A warning message 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' followed by the Account ID is displayed, and processing continues without a valid card number — the program does not stop or abort

all_rules.Rule_Name: Warn When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account ID does not exist in the Cross-Reference file, a warning must be displayed identifying the missing account. Processing continues without a valid card number rather than stopping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference file lookup was successful and the card cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) has been retrieved containing the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An interest transaction record is being written for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) retrieved from the Cross-Reference file is assigned to the transaction card number field (TRAN-CARD-NUM) on the interest transaction record being written to the Transaction output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Card Number for Interest Transaction Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid cross-reference record is found, the card number associated with the account is retained and must be used when writing interest transaction records for that account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record is being processed with a known Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the Disclosure Group file using the composite key of Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the interest rate record associated with that specific combination from the Disclosure Group file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Look Up Interest Rate by Account Group, Transaction Type, and Transaction Category
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the applicable interest rate from the Disclosure Group file using a composite key made up of the account's group ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Disclosure Group file using Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A matching disclosure group record is found for the specific Account Group ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate from the matched record is retrieved and used as the applicable rate for the current transaction category balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Specific Group Interest Rate When Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Disclosure Group file contains a matching record for the account's specific group, transaction type, and transaction category combination, the interest rate from that record is used for interest calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Disclosure Group file using the account's specific Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching record is found for the specific Account Group ID (record not found condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system replaces the Account Group ID with the value 'DEFAULT' and retries the lookup on the Disclosure Group file using the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fallback to DEFAULT Group When Specific Account Group Rate Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no interest rate record exists in the Disclosure Group file for the account's specific group, the system retries the lookup using the reserved group code 'DEFAULT' while keeping the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has retried the Disclosure Group file lookup using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID with the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A matching record is found for the 'DEFAULT' group
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate from the DEFAULT group record is retrieved and used as the applicable rate for the current transaction category balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Default Interest Rate When DEFAULT Group Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Disclosure Group file contains a record for the 'DEFAULT' group with the matching transaction type and category codes, the default interest rate is retrieved and applied to the transaction category balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has retried the Disclosure Group file lookup using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching record is found for the 'DEFAULT' group either
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate value remains zero, indicating that no applicable interest rate exists for this transaction category balance combination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Interest Rate Remains Zero When DEFAULT Group Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither the specific account group nor the DEFAULT group has a matching interest rate record in the Disclosure Group file, the interest rate remains at zero, indicating no interest is applicable for this transaction category balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest rate lookup has been completed for the current transaction category balance record using either the specific Account Group ID or the DEFAULT group
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The retrieved interest rate is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips interest calculation and fee computation entirely for this transaction category balance record and proceeds to the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Interest Calculation When Interest Rate Is Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the retrieved interest rate (from either the specific group or the DEFAULT group) is zero, the system skips both interest calculation and fee computation for that transaction category balance record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest rate lookup has been completed for the current transaction category balance record using either the specific Account Group ID or the DEFAULT group
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The retrieved interest rate is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to perform interest calculation followed by fee computation for the current transaction category balance record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Interest Calculation When Interest Rate Is Greater Than Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the retrieved interest rate is greater than zero, the system proceeds to compute the monthly interest and applicable fees for the current transaction category balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record is being processed, and the Account Group ID has been retrieved from the Account Master record, and the Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code are available from the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the Disclosure Group file using the composite key of Account Group ID + Transaction Type Code + Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) associated with that specific combination of Account Group, Transaction Type, and Transaction Category from the Disclosure Group file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lookup Interest Rate by Account Group, Transaction Type, and Transaction Category
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction category balance record being processed, the system must retrieve the applicable interest rate from the Disclosure Group file using the account's group identifier combined with the transaction type code and transaction category code as a composite lookup key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the Disclosure Group file using the account's specific Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Disclosure Group file lookup completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching record is found, the interest rate from that specific group record is used for interest calculation; if no matching record is found (record not found condition), the system initiates the default interest rate fallback process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether Specific Disclosure Group Record Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to retrieve the interest rate for the account's specific group, the system must determine whether a matching disclosure group record was found or not, in order to decide whether to use the specific rate or fall back to a default rate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group file lookup using the account's specific Account Group ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code has returned a matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The specific disclosure group record is successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) from the specific group record is used as-is for the subsequent interest computation for that transaction category balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Interest Rate from Account's Specific Disclosure Group Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a disclosure group record is found matching the account's own group, transaction type, and transaction category, the interest rate from that specific record is used directly for the interest calculation without any fallback.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group file lookup using the account's specific Account Group ID returned no matching record (record not found)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the specific group record is missing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Group ID used for the disclosure group lookup is overridden and set to the literal value 'DEFAULT', replacing the account's own group identifier, and a warning message 'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING' followed by 'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Override Account Group ID with DEFAULT When Specific Group Record Is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no disclosure group record exists for the account's specific group, the system must override the account's group identifier with the literal value 'DEFAULT' before attempting a second lookup, ensuring a fallback rate can be retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Group ID has been set to 'DEFAULT' because no specific group record was found, and the Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code remain unchanged from the original transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a second lookup on the Disclosure Group file using the composite key of 'DEFAULT' + Transaction Type Code + Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the default interest rate record from the Disclosure Group file for that Transaction Type and Transaction Category combination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Disclosure Group File Using DEFAULT Group Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting the group identifier to 'DEFAULT', the system performs a second lookup on the Disclosure Group file using the DEFAULT group code combined with the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code from the original record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the Disclosure Group file using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID, with the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DEFAULT group Disclosure Group file lookup completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching default record is found, the interest rate from the DEFAULT group record is used for interest calculation; if the default record is also not found, the interest rate remains at zero and no interest is charged for that transaction category balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether Default Disclosure Group Record Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to retrieve the interest rate using the DEFAULT group code, the system must determine whether a default disclosure group record was found, in order to either apply the default rate or treat the interest rate as zero for that transaction category.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group file lookup using 'DEFAULT' as the Account Group ID, with the same Transaction Type Code and Transaction Category Code, has returned a matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DEFAULT disclosure group record is successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) from the DEFAULT group record is used for the subsequent interest computation for that transaction category balance, in place of the account's specific group rate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Interest Rate from DEFAULT Disclosure Group Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the DEFAULT disclosure group record is successfully found, the interest rate from that default record is used for the interest calculation, serving as the fallback rate for accounts whose specific group has no defined rate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The interest rate (DIS-INT-RATE) retrieved from the Disclosure Group file for the current transaction category balance record is zero, either because the rate is explicitly set to zero in the disclosure group record or because no applicable disclosure group record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the retrieved interest rate value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips both the interest computation and the fee computation for that transaction category balance record, no interest transaction is written to the Transaction file, and no interest amount is added to the account's total interest accumulator for that category

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Zero Interest Rate When No Disclosure Group Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the interest rate retrieved from the Disclosure Group file (either specific or default) is zero, no interest calculation and no fee computation is performed for that transaction category balance record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been read with a valid Transaction Category Balance amount (TRAN-CAT-BAL), AND an Annual Interest Rate (DIS-INT-RATE) has been retrieved from the Disclosure Group file for the matching Account Group, Transaction Category Code, and Transaction Type Code combination, AND the Annual Interest Rate is not zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The monthly interest calculation is triggered for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Monthly Interest Amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) is computed as: (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) divided by 1200, where dividing by 1200 converts the annual percentage rate into a monthly decimal rate applied to the balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Interest Amount Calculation Using Annual Rate
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction category balance record with a non-zero interest rate, the system calculates the monthly interest charge by applying the standard monthly interest formula using the transaction category balance and the annual interest rate retrieved from the Disclosure Group.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Monthly Interest Amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been successfully calculated for the current transaction category balance record, AND a running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) exists for the current account, which was reset to zero when processing for this account began
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The monthly interest amount is ready to be consolidated at the account level
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Monthly Interest Amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) is added to the Running Account Total Interest (WS-TOTAL-INT), so that WS-TOTAL-INT reflects the cumulative interest across all transaction categories processed so far for the current account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accumulate Monthly Interest Into Running Account Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: After computing the monthly interest for a single transaction category balance record, the system adds that amount to the running total interest accumulator for the current account. This accumulator collects interest across all transaction categories and types belonging to the same account before the account balance is finally updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A monthly interest amount has been computed for a transaction category balance record, AND a date parameter (PARM-DATE) is available as input to the program, AND a transaction ID suffix counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) is maintained across all interest transactions written during the program run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A new interest transaction record is about to be created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction ID suffix counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) is incremented by 1, AND the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is formed by concatenating the date parameter (PARM-DATE) and the incremented suffix (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), producing a unique identifier for this interest transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate Unique Transaction ID for Interest Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each interest transaction written to the Transaction File must carry a unique Transaction ID formed by combining the processing date parameter with an auto-incremented numeric suffix, ensuring every interest charge is individually identifiable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A unique Transaction ID has been generated for the interest transaction, AND the Monthly Interest Amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been computed, AND the Account ID (ACCT-ID) is available from the Account Master record, AND the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The interest transaction record is being assembled for writing to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record is populated with the following values: Transaction Type Code set to '01', Transaction Category Code set to '05', Transaction Source set to 'System', Transaction Description set to 'Int. for a/c ' concatenated with the Account ID, Transaction Amount set to the computed Monthly Interest Amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT), Merchant ID set to zero, Merchant Name set to blank, Merchant City set to blank, Merchant ZIP set to blank, AND Card Number set to the card number retrieved from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate System-Generated Interest Transaction Record Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When writing an interest transaction to the Transaction File, the system populates all required transaction fields with system-defined values identifying it as a system-generated interest charge, including transaction classification codes, source, description, amount, and card reference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest transaction record is being assembled with all required business fields populated, AND the current system date and time is accessible
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction timestamps are being assigned before writing the record to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time is captured and formatted as a standard timestamp (DB2-FORMAT-TS), AND both the Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) and the Transaction Processing Timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS) are set to this same current system timestamp value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Current System Timestamp to Interest Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the origination timestamp and the processing timestamp of the interest transaction record must reflect the current system date and time at the moment the transaction is created, ensuring an accurate audit trail for system-generated interest charges.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All fields of the interest transaction record (TRAN-RECORD) have been fully populated including Transaction ID, type codes, source, description, amount, merchant fields, card number, and timestamps
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The completed interest transaction record is submitted for writing to the Transaction Output File (TRANSACT-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record is successfully written to the Transaction Output File, AND processing continues to the next transaction category balance record; OR if the write to the Transaction Output File fails, the system raises a business error indicating that the interest transaction record could not be recorded, and halts further processing to prevent data inconsistency

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Completed Interest Transaction Record to Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all fields of the interest transaction record have been populated, the complete record must be written to the Transaction Output File. If the write operation fails, the transaction cannot be recorded and the process must be halted to prevent incomplete interest postings.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is processing transaction category balance records sequentially and detects that the current record's Account ID is different from the previously tracked Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A new account is identified for the first time or after completing all categories for the prior account
