Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) is reset to zero, ensuring that interest accumulation starts fresh for the new account with no carry-over from any previously processed account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Interest Accumulator When New Account Processing Begins
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new account is encountered in the transaction category balance file, the running total interest accumulator must be reset to zero before processing begins for that account, ensuring interest from a prior account does not carry over.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been processed for the current account, a non-zero interest rate was found in the Disclosure Group file, and the monthly interest amount has been computed as (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) / 1200
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The monthly interest computation step completes successfully for the current transaction category
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The computed monthly interest amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) is added to the running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) for the current account, so that Running Total Interest = Previous Running Total + Monthly Interest for this category

all_rules.Rule_Name: Add Computed Monthly Interest to Running Account Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction category balance record where a non-zero interest rate exists and monthly interest has been computed, the computed monthly interest amount is added to the running total interest for the current account. This accumulates interest contributions from each transaction category.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has processed at least one transaction category balance record for the current account and has added its monthly interest to the running total
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The next transaction category balance record is read and its Account ID matches the currently tracked Account ID (WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program continues processing the new record for the same account — it looks up the interest rate for the new transaction category and type combination, computes monthly interest if the rate is non-zero, and adds it to the same running total accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT), without resetting the accumulator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Interest Accumulation Across All Transaction Categories for the Same Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program continues to read and process additional transaction category balance records for the same account, accumulating interest for each category, until either a new account ID is encountered or the end of the file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records for the current account have been processed and monthly interest has been computed and accumulated for each applicable category
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either a new Account ID is detected on the next record or the end of the transaction category balance file is reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running total interest accumulator (WS-TOTAL-INT) represents the total interest owed across all transaction categories for the account, and this cumulative total is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) when the account record is updated and saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Recognize Completion of Interest Accumulation Across All Categories for an Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all transaction category balance records for a given account have been processed, the running total interest accumulator holds the cumulative interest across all transaction categories and types for that account. This final total is then applied to the account's current balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest charge is being recorded for a transaction category balance record, and the current processing date (PARM-DATE) and a running sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A new interest transaction record is about to be created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) is incremented by 1, and the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is formed by concatenating the processing date (PARM-DATE) with the updated sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), ensuring each transaction has a unique identifier across the processing run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate Unique Transaction ID for Interest Charge
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each interest charge transaction must be assigned a unique transaction identifier formed by combining the processing date parameter with an auto-incremented sequence number suffix.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed for a computed monthly interest charge
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction type is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TRAN-TYPE-CD) is set to '01', designating the transaction as an Interest Charge type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Interest Transaction with Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: All system-generated interest charge transactions must be classified with Transaction Type Code '01' to identify them as interest charge transactions in the transaction output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed for a computed monthly interest charge
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction category is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Code (TRAN-CAT-CD) is set to '05', designating the transaction as belonging to the Interest Category

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Interest Category Code to Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: All system-generated interest charge transactions must be assigned Transaction Category Code '05' to categorize them under the Interest Category in the transaction output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed for a computed monthly interest charge
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction source is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Source (TRAN-SOURCE) is set to the value 'System', indicating the transaction was generated automatically by the system and not initiated by a customer or merchant

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify System as the Source of Interest Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: All interest charge transactions generated by this program must be identified as system-originated by setting the transaction source to 'System', distinguishing them from customer-initiated or merchant-initiated transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed and the Account ID (ACCT-ID) of the account being processed is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction description is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description (TRAN-DESC) is set by concatenating the literal text 'Int. for a/c ' with the Account ID (ACCT-ID), producing a description such as 'Int. for a/c 1234567890' that clearly identifies the account associated with the interest charge

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Descriptive Label Referencing Account for Interest Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each interest transaction must carry a human-readable description that identifies it as an interest charge and references the specific account for which the interest was calculated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The monthly interest amount (WS-MONTHLY-INT) has been computed as (Transaction Category Balance × Annual Interest Rate) / 1200 for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction amount is being assigned to the interest transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount (TRAN-AMT) is set to the computed monthly interest value (WS-MONTHLY-INT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Computed Monthly Interest as Transaction Amount
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction amount for each interest charge record must reflect the exact monthly interest amount computed for that transaction category balance, ensuring the financial value recorded is accurate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) has been retrieved for the current account using the Account ID, and the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number is being assigned to the interest transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Card Number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is set to the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Associate Card Number from Cross-Reference with Interest Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each interest transaction must be linked to the card number associated with the account, retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record that was looked up when the account was first encountered during processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new interest transaction record is being constructed for a system-generated interest charge
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The merchant details are being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant ID (TRAN-MERCHANT-ID) is set to 0, and the Merchant Name (TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME), Merchant City (TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY), and Merchant ZIP Code (TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP) are all set to blank spaces, indicating no merchant is associated with this interest charge

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Merchant Details for System-Generated Interest Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Since interest charges are system-generated and not associated with any merchant, all merchant-related fields on the interest transaction record must be set to empty or zero values to indicate that no merchant is involved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An interest transaction record is being prepared for writing to the transaction output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The timestamp is being captured for the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time is retrieved and formatted into a standard timestamp format (DB2-FORMAT-TS) containing year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds components, ready to be applied to the transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current System Date and Time for Transaction Timestamping
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date and time must be captured at the moment the interest transaction is being created, to be used as both the origination and processing timestamps on the transaction record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date and time has been captured and formatted into the standard timestamp (DB2-FORMAT-TS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The timestamps are being assigned to the interest transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) and the Transaction Processing Timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS) are set to the same current formatted timestamp value (DB2-FORMAT-TS), indicating the transaction was originated and processed at the same time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stamp Interest Transaction with Origination and Processing Timestamps
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the origination timestamp and the processing timestamp on the interest transaction record must be set to the same current date-time value, reflecting that the transaction was both originated and processed at the same point in time by the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All fields of the interest transaction record (TRAN-RECORD) have been fully populated including transaction ID, type, category, source, description, amount, card number, merchant details, and timestamps
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The completed interest transaction record is submitted for writing to the Transaction Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record (FD-TRANFILE-REC) is successfully written to the Transaction Output File, and the transaction is permanently recorded as an interest charge for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Completed Interest Transaction Record to Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all fields of the interest transaction record have been populated, the complete record must be written to the Transaction Output File to permanently record the interest charge.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to generate a unique Transaction ID for a new interest transaction record, and a running sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) holds the value from the previously generated transaction (or zero if this is the first transaction in the run)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A new interest transaction is ready to be written to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) must be incremented by exactly 1 before the Transaction ID is formed, so that each transaction in the same processing run receives a strictly increasing, unique numeric suffix

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Transaction Sequence Counter Before ID Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time an interest transaction is to be recorded, the system increments a running sequence counter by 1 to ensure each transaction receives a unique sequential number within the processing run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Processing Date parameter (PARM-DATE) has been provided to the program at runtime representing the date of the processing run, and the sequence counter (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX) has just been incremented by 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system constructs the Transaction ID for the current interest transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) must be formed by concatenating the full Processing Date (PARM-DATE) immediately followed by the current sequence counter value (WS-TRANID-SUFFIX), with both values used at their full defined sizes without truncation or delimiter separation, resulting in a composite identifier such as '2024121500002'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Combine Processing Date and Sequence Number to Form Unique Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The unique Transaction ID is constructed by concatenating the Processing Date parameter (passed into the program at runtime) with the incremented sequence counter, forming a single composite identifier that is unique within the processing run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A unique Transaction ID has been successfully generated by combining the Processing Date and the incremented sequence counter into TRAN-ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates all fields of the interest Transaction Record prior to writing it to the Transaction Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The generated Transaction ID value stored in TRAN-ID must be included as part of the Transaction Record (TRAN-RECORD) that is written to the Transaction Output File, ensuring the transaction is permanently recorded with its unique identifier

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Generated Transaction ID in the Interest Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the unique Transaction ID has been generated, it is stored in the Transaction Record field (TRAN-ID) so that it is available as part of the complete transaction record that will be written to the Transaction Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction category balance record has been processed, a non-zero interest rate was found for the account group, transaction category code, and transaction type code combination, and the monthly interest has already been computed and accumulated for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fee computation step is invoked as the next action following interest calculation for the current transaction category balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No fee calculation is performed and no fee transaction record is written; the process completes without any changes to account balances, transaction records, or any other business data, and control returns to the main processing loop to continue with the next transaction category balance record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fee Computation Reserved for Future Implementation
all_rules.Rule_Description: This rule defines the fee calculation step as a placeholder process that is invoked after interest computation for a transaction category balance record where a non-zero interest rate exists. No fee logic is currently implemented; the step is reserved for future business fee computation per transaction category.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered either because a new account ID was detected in the transaction category balance file or the end of the transaction category balance file has been reached, AND the total interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT) has been accumulated across all transaction category balance records processed for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account balance update process is executed for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) must be increased by the total accumulated interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT), resulting in a new current balance equal to the prior current balance plus the total interest calculated for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Add Total Calculated Interest to Account Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account balance update is triggered, the total interest accumulated across all transaction categories for the account during the current cycle is added to the account's existing current balance to produce the new updated balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered for the current account, AND the total interest has already been added to the account's current balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is being prepared for saving back to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) on the account record must be set to zero, indicating that all credit activity for the current cycle has been processed and the cycle credit balance is cleared

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Current Cycle Credit Amount to Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the end-of-cycle account update, the current cycle credit amount on the account record is cleared to zero, signifying that the credit activity for the current billing cycle has been fully processed and the cycle is being closed out.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account balance update has been triggered for the current account, AND the total interest has been added to the account's current balance, AND the current cycle credit amount has already been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is being prepared for saving back to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) on the account record must be set to zero, indicating that all debit activity for the current cycle has been processed and the cycle debit balance is cleared

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Current Cycle Debit Amount to Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the end-of-cycle account update, the current cycle debit amount on the account record is cleared to zero, signifying that the debit activity for the current billing cycle has been fully processed and the cycle is being closed out.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been updated with the new current balance (original balance plus total interest), the current cycle credit amount has been set to zero, and the current cycle debit amount has been set to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record update is written back to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete updated account record must be saved to the Account Master File, replacing the existing account record for that account ID, so that the new balance and cleared cycle amounts are permanently recorded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated Account Record to Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the account's current balance has been updated with total interest and the current cycle credit and debit amounts have been reset to zero, the updated account record must be persisted back to the Account Master File to make the changes permanent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to save the updated account record (with new balance and zeroed cycle amounts) back to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The result of the account record save operation is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record was saved successfully, processing continues to the next step; If the account record was NOT saved successfully, an error message 'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE' is displayed and the program immediately stops all processing, as continuing with an unrecorded account balance update would result in data integrity issues

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account Record Successfully Updated in Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to save the updated account record to the Account Master File, the outcome of the save operation must be validated. If the save was not successful, the program must stop processing immediately to prevent data inconsistency, as the account balance update is a critical operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is processing transaction category balance records sequentially, AND at least one account has been fully processed (i.e., this is not the very first account encountered in the file)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either (a) the Account ID on the current transaction category balance record is different from the Account ID of the previously processed record, indicating a new account group has started, OR (b) the end of the transaction category balance file has been reached, indicating the last account's records have all been read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account balance update process must be invoked for the account that was just completed, applying the total accumulated interest to its balance and resetting its cycle credit and debit amounts to zero before beginning processing for the new account or before closing the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Account Balance Update on New Account Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account balance update process must be triggered at the correct point in processing — either when a new account ID is encountered in the transaction category balance file (indicating all records for the prior account have been read) or when the end of the transaction category balance file is reached (ensuring the last account is also updated).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been reading Transaction Category Balance records sequentially and has now reached the end of the Transaction Category Balance file, and the end-of-file condition is set to 'Y'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected within the main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If at least one account was previously processed during this run (i.e., the first-time processing flag was set to 'N', meaning at least one account record was encountered), the final account update procedure must be invoked to finalize that account's data; if no accounts were processed (file was empty and first-time flag remains 'Y'), no account update is performed and processing proceeds directly to closing all files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Final Account Update Upon End of Transaction Category Balance File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the Transaction Category Balance file is reached, the program must determine whether at least one account was processed during the run. If at least one account was processed, the final account's accumulated data must be updated. If no accounts were processed (file was empty), no update action is taken and processing proceeds directly to closing all files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The final account update has been triggered for the last processed account, and the total accumulated interest (WS-TOTAL-INT) has been computed by summing monthly interest charges across all transaction categories and transaction types for that account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total accumulated interest amount (WS-TOTAL-INT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), increasing the balance by the full interest amount owed for the current cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Total Accumulated Interest to Account Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the final account update, the total interest amount accumulated across all transaction category balance records for the last processed account must be added to that account's current balance in the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is being executed for the last processed account, and the total accumulated interest has already been applied to the account's current balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current cycle credit reset step is performed within the account update procedure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account's current cycle credit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is set to zero, clearing all credit activity recorded for the current billing cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Current Cycle Credit Amount to Zero on Account Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the final account update, the current billing cycle's total credit amount for the account must be reset to zero, signifying that the cycle's credit activity has been fully processed and the account is ready for the next billing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account balance update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is being executed for the last processed account, and both the interest has been applied to the current balance and the current cycle credit amount has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current cycle debit reset step is performed within the account update procedure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account's current cycle debit amount (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is set to zero, clearing all debit activity recorded for the current billing cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Current Cycle Debit Amount to Zero on Account Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the final account update, the current billing cycle's total debit amount for the account must be reset to zero, signifying that the cycle's debit activity has been fully processed and the account is ready for the next billing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update procedure (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) has completed applying total accumulated interest to the current balance and has reset both the current cycle credit amount and current cycle debit amount to zero for the last processed account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save step is executed to persist the updated account data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated account record — containing the new current balance (with interest applied), zero current cycle credit amount, and zero current cycle debit amount — is written back to the Account Master File by rewriting the existing account record; if the save is successful, processing proceeds to close all files; if the save fails, an account file write error is reported and the program terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Updated Account Record to Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After applying the accumulated interest to the current balance and resetting the current cycle credit and debit amounts, the updated account record must be saved back to the Account Master File to make the changes permanent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction category balance records have been fully processed and the last account update has been applied
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program has finished its main processing loop and is ready to shut down
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C' to signal successful completion of all business processing before any file closure begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of all processing, the program announces its end of execution before closing any files, providing an audit trail of program lifecycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has displayed its end-of-execution message and is proceeding with the shutdown sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Transaction Category Balance file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Balance file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION BALANCE FILE' error and terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Transaction Category Balance File on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Category Balance input file must be properly closed as the first file closure step during program completion to ensure data integrity and release file resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Balance file has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING CROSS REF FILE' error and terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Cross-Reference File on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Cross-Reference input file must be properly closed as the second file closure step during program completion, following the closure of the Transaction Category Balance file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference file has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Disclosure Group file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Disclosure Group file must be successfully closed; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' error and terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Disclosure Group File on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Disclosure Group input file, which holds interest rate data, must be properly closed as the third file closure step during program completion, following the closure of the Cross-Reference file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group file has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master file must be successfully closed, ensuring all account balance updates and cycle resets written during processing are preserved; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' error and terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Account Master File on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master file, which was opened for both reading and updating, must be properly closed as the fourth file closure step during program completion to ensure all account balance updates are committed and the file is properly released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master file has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Transaction output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction output file must be successfully closed, ensuring all interest transaction records written during processing are preserved and available; if the closure fails, the program must report a 'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION FILE' error and terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Transaction Output File on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction output file, which holds all newly generated interest transaction records, must be properly closed as the fifth and final file closure step during program completion to ensure all written interest transactions are committed and available for downstream processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed all transaction category balance record processing including the final account update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program enters its completion phase
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All five files must be closed in the following strict order: (1) Transaction Category Balance file, (2) Cross-Reference file, (3) Disclosure Group file, (4) Account Master file, (5) Transaction Output file; each file must be successfully closed before the next closure is attempted; if any file closure fails, the program must report the specific file error and terminate abnormally without proceeding to close remaining files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mandatory Sequential File Closure Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: All five files used by the program must be closed in a strict mandatory sequence during program completion: Transaction Category Balance → Cross-Reference → Disclosure Group → Account Master → Transaction Output. This sequence ensures orderly shutdown and data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All five files — Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, and Transaction Output — have been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program has completed all shutdown steps
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must return control to the calling environment (GOBACK), indicating that all interest calculations, account balance updates, cycle credit and debit resets, and interest transaction record writes have been completed successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Successful Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all files have been successfully closed, the program must return control to the calling environment, signaling successful and complete execution of all interest calculation and account update business processing.

description:
CBACT04C is a batch interest calculator program within the CardDemo application that reads transaction category balance records sequentially, retrieves corresponding account and cross-reference data, looks up applicable interest rates from a disclosure group file, computes monthly interest charges per transaction category, and updates account balances while writing interest transaction records to an output file. The program processes records grouped by account, accumulating total interest per account before applying the final balance update. It is a standalone batch driver program that receives a date parameter via the Linkage Section and orchestrates all processing internally.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM/FILE - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Open all required files (Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, and Transaction output files) to prepare for interest calculation processing 2: Transaction Category Balance Record Reading - Sequentially read each transaction category balance record one at a time to drive the interest calculation process 3: Account Change Detection - Detect when the account ID changes between consecutive transaction category balance records to trigger account-level processing 4: Account Interest Accumulation Reset - When a new account is encountered, reset the total interest accumulator to zero before processing the new account's categories 5: Account Data Retrieval - Retrieve the full account details (current balance, credit/debit cycle amounts, account group ID, etc.) from the Account Master file using the account ID 6: Card Cross-Reference Lookup - Retrieve the card number associated with the account by looking up the Cross-Reference file using the account ID, to be used when writing interest transactions 7: Interest Rate Lookup by Account Group - Look up the applicable interest rate from the Disclosure Group file using the account's group ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code 8: Default Interest Rate Fallback - When no specific disclosure group record is found for the account group, fall back to retrieving the interest rate using a 'DEFAULT' group code 9: Monthly Interest Calculation - Calculate the monthly interest charge for a transaction category by applying the formula: (Transaction Category Balance × Interest Rate) / 1200 10: Total Interest Accumulation - Add the computed monthly interest for each transaction category to the running total interest amount for the current account 11: Interest Transaction Record Creation - Create and write a new transaction record for each interest charge, including transaction ID (date + sequence suffix), type code '01', category code '05', source 'System', description referencing the account, interest amount, card number, and timestamps 12: Transaction ID Generation - Generate a unique transaction ID by combining the processing date (passed as a parameter) with an incrementing numeric suffix 13: Fee Calculation - Placeholder process reserved for future implementation of fee computation per transaction category (currently not implemented) 14: Account Balance Update - After processing all transaction categories for an account, update the account record by adding the total calculated interest to the current balance and resetting the current cycle credit and debit amounts to zero 15: Final Account Update - After reaching end-of-file on the transaction category balance file, perform the account balance update for the last account processed 16: Program Completion - Close all opened files (Transaction Category Balance, Cross-Reference, Disclosure Group, Account Master, and Transaction files) and end program execution
